checks.note: Access tokens page confirms vcp_ prefix, Bearer header, full-account/team/project scopes, expiration. Sign in with Vercel Tokens page confirms the OAuth access token (vca_) is used to authenticate REST API requests, 1-hour access token, 30-day rotating refresh token. So OAuth2 is for API access, not only login. The cited access-tokens page does not cover OAuth, so the Tokens page is added as evidence. PKCE was not verified on a fetched page.

Prerequisite is only a Vercel account. No paid tier or review step is stated. Some teams require 2FA/SAML. The Hobby plan terms and rate limit values were not read in detail. The limits page exists with a REST API rate limits section.
The REST API reference lists a large endpoint catalog (access groups, deployments, projects, etc.), with endpoints on api.vercel.com. REST only. Breadth is broad.

The page states 'Vercel MCP is Vercel's official MCP server' at https://mcp.vercel.com, with OAuth. Clients must use CIMD or be reviewed and approved. The page now lives at /docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp. The cited /docs/mcp/vercel-mcp path is replaced with the canonical URL.
Self-serve token, REST API, official MCP. No blocker found. Remaining caveats are rate limits and OAuth scope coverage, which are minor.

corrected.one_liner: Vercel is a frontend cloud platform for deploying, hosting and managing web projects, with deployments, domains, env vars, logs and analytics.
corrected.auth_notes: Access tokens (prefix vcp_) are created on the Account Tokens page, or via API/CLI. They can be scoped to full account, a team, or a single project, with an expiration, and are sent as "Authorization: Bearer". OAuth 2.0 / OIDC via "Sign in with Vercel" lets a third-party app obtain an opaque access token (vca_, valid 1 hour) plus a 30-day single-use rotating refresh token, used as a Bearer token to call the REST API on the user's behalf. PKCE was not verified on a fetched page. The scopes page was not fetched, so REST coverage for OAuth tokens is unverified. The official MCP server uses OAuth.
corrected.access_notes: A Vercel account is enough to create a token, and the docs don't mention a paid tier for the API. Hobby plan terms and REST API rate limit values were not reviewed (a 429 is documented, see /docs/limits#rate-limits). Some teams require 2FA or SAML before a token can be scoped to them. OAuth apps are created from the dashboard, and the docs list no review step. For MCP, clients need to use CIMD or be reviewed and approved by Vercel.
corrected.blocker: none. Minor caveats: OAuth scope coverage of the REST API is unverified, and rate limits were not reviewed.
